text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills This is not up to the typical quality of Melissa and Doug products in my opinion. There are 12 mini-projects in this "book"(it's an scruffy bubble envelope with other envelopes inside), and each has some very basic scissor projects. The first one, for instance, has your child cutting in straight lines to create a simple memory game. The second one builds on this, adding some cross-cutting, and so forth.

Each kit is good enough, and the variety is greatly appreciated by the kiddos. In some instances, the instructions needed a little work, while in others, they were perfect. In each case, they're language independent and entirely taught through pictures, which is great for helping the kiddos follow along and do the projects somewhat independently.

There are two pairs of scissors included in this package - a straight pair, and a "scrapbooking" scissor that cuts "teeth" - but these safety scissors are entirely too "safety" for me. The straight one works well enough at first, while the teeth scissors barely worked at all. Their entirely plastic frame wears out with minimal use. There are no metal parts on them, outside of the screws. We had trouble making clean cuts as we approached the middle of the kits, and by the end, we just switched to metal scissors as we were mangling the paper more than doing actual cutting.

The problem with the scissors, as well as the complete lack of a storage solution for these projects as they're in progress is enough for me to rate this kit lower than I normally do. My kit arrived mispacked, so I received two #4 projects, and no #3 project. Good projects can be had here, but bring some of your own materials.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills

It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

So the puzzle itself isn’t super high res, nor are the pieces particularly inventive in how they’re cut, but man am I having fun reliving the show. Honestly, this is all about the nostalgia and having a chill time. It’s a little harder than I expected, but still totally doable. Perfect escape!

I usually look at sets from an AFOL’s (adult fan of Lego) perspective, which is admittedly different than a kid’s. I usually want my sets to look cool on display and/or have a fun building experience. Lego building is great fun and stress relief even when you’re an adult.

Anyway, I think this set looks like it was released during my childhood, twenty years ago. It’s bland and basic, a bunch of rectangles plopped on top of each other. Even the police car and search truck look like boxes on wheels.

That said, there are a few things I like about the set. I like the drone, the exploding cell, the searchlight, and the table tennis (though I was disappointed the table uses stickers). BlueFit German Tiger I Panzer Tank with Remote Control, Battery, Light, Sound, Rotating Turret and Recoil Action When Cannon Artillery Shoots, Mini 1:72 Scale, Assorted Color This this is awesome. For something that easily sits on the palm of your hand the detail is pretty sharp. It honestly looks like a World War ][ Tiger tank with tons of details. I received the standard, mostly green, camouflage there's also a darker camouflage and a blue tank available. Colors appear to ship randomly. Remote control device coloring also seem to match the tank you get.
This little thing really zips around. I was surprised at how quick it gets up and goes. There's also a super speed button on the controller that adds fifty percent to the speed of the tank. There's also engine noises and what I'm guessing are 'track' sounds are this races around. The turret will turn 360° in one direction, I found going one way the barrel would hang up on the antenna but the turret rotation switches back and forth as you rotate. The barrel also raises and lowers as the turret turns. When you press the fire button there's the sound of a cannon firing and the entire tank body recoils backwards.
The remote control takes four double A batteries and the tank itself charges from a cable attached to the side of the remote. Charging time is fairly quick and I've already gotten several hours of fun out of the tank and it's still going strong. The only reason I can't give it four stars is the tank just won't drive in a straight line. You can someone adjust for the tendency to turn by steering left or right as you go but it would have been just that much cooler if it had driven in a straight line. Still, I'm a fully grown adult and this is one of my favorite things. It's just such a gas to play with.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game

text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy This is very cute! Elmo is soft red plush, with big "googly" eyes, a big orange "squeezable" fabric nose, and a bright yellow shirt with a white, plastic-coated star, outlined in blue, with white surround sound waves.

The white star on the shirt shows the spot where you must press a button to "tickle Elmo's tummy" (to activate each sequence) but it is placed just a bit high. To press the center of the button, I have to place my thumb below the star, on the yellow shirt fabric.

My favorite feature is how Elmo's mouth opens and closes while the talking and singing sounds are playing. Incredible engineering and technology went into this toy!

This toy is targeted to ages "2-4 Years." A child has to put one of Elmo's 3 hats on his head for each different play mode. Some 2-year-olds will no doubt have hands large enough to accommodate holding the hats and pushing the plastic tab down into the slot between Elmo's eyes, but some will need assistance.

The toy is packaged in "try me" mode. You can reach through a hole in the front of the box and "tickle Elmo's tummy." When you bring Elmo home, pull the fabric on the bottom to the side, move the switch from "try me" to "on." Then pull the fabric back up and attach with the Velcro strip. Batteries are held firmly in this bottom compartment with a tightly screwed on lid. Requires 4 AA batteries.

4 INTERACTIVE PLAY MODES:

HAT-FREE. I think Elmo is saying, "Hi, hello! Elmo likes to imagine with you, what should we imagine today?" "Place a hat on Elmo's head so we can imagine together." "Let's play together, tickle Elmo's tummy." "Let's play together, squeeze Elmo's nose."
Squeezing Elmo's nose gives different responses, sometimes it's two honks, and sometimes it's a long squeak.

PRINCE ELMO
"Greetings loyal friend, Elmo loves wearing a crown." "Prince Elmo says, bounce Elmo." Elmo has to be "bounced" fairly hard and there is a "boing, boing, boing" sound, followed by, "Squeeze Elmo's nose." After his nose is squeezed, he says, "You did it! Tickle Elmo's tummy." After button on tummy is pushed, he says, "You did it! "Now, first, squeeze Elmo's nose, then bounce Elmo."

If you don't do it right, there's a sound, followed by, "That's not right. First squeeze Elmo's nose, then bounce Elmo."

Elmo asks for three correct actions in a row (squeeze his nose, tickle his tummy, or bounce him). After three correct actions in a row, he'll up the challenge to a two-action sequence.

It's repetitive, with immediate positive or negative feedback.

CAPTAIN COWBOY
"Well howdy partner, hello to Captain Cowboy, yee haa!"
"How many times can you squeeze Elmo's nose?" "Let's bounce together."
Squeeze Elmo's nose and he counts to 20.
Elmo sings a song.

CAPTAIN ELMO
"Squeeze Elmo's tummy to hear a song." Elmo sings a song ("Sailing, sailing over the ocean blue, Captain Elmo loves to listen to all of the sounds, don't you?") and plays a game with sea sounds: a horn, seagull, bell or dolphin. "Squeeze Elmo's tummy when you hear a horn," (or seagull, bell, or dolphin). When Elmo's tummy is squeezed, there is immediate positive feedback: the sound of a xylophone.

This is fun and interactive. Parents can model patience when they show children how to put Elmo's hats on him. Parents can watch their children learn, or play and sing along. Parents can learn about their child's temperament (easy, difficult, slow-to-warm-up) when they see their child's response to Elmo. Some children will be able to play with Elmo by themselves. For some adults, the pitch of his voice and the repetitive sounds could begin to chafe after awhile.

Through 3/31/2015, there is an insert included in the box, advertising, "Elmo the Musical," and a web address for parents and children to watch an episode online.
text_fidelity_b: Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy

Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+ If you, like me, are looking for games to play with a high energy, lack of focus little boy, then this is the game for you. For my four year old, games with a lot of rules and that require skills he's still learning with clear winners and losers are not the best choice games for us. He doesn't have the patience, skill, or temperament. I needed games to slowly introduce him into those skills and Pop Up Pirate is that game! The only rule, everyone takes turns to place a sword into a slot. The person who makes the pirate pop-up out of the barrel wins. We don't play winner/loser, but you can if you choose to do so.

The game comes with 20 swords, four colors with five each, a barrel, and said pirate. It's for 2 to 4 players, my son and I just pick up a sword no matter the color, but if you have more kids or players, then you can choose colors. You stick the pirate in the barrel where there is a trap/spring mechanism that is only triggered when someone sticks a sword in the right slot. Each player takes a color and everyone takes turns sticking a sword into a slot. When the right sword pokes the pirate, he pops high up into the air. The pirate is fairly light weight so if he were to really go flying he would not break anything or hurt anyone. The pirate jumps at most 2 feet into the air, probably less. The only caveat is to make kids aren't sticking their face near the barrel with the pirate in the hole for obvious reasons. This game comes in fairly big box as the barrel is about as wide as a clothes iron, but not nearly as tall.

If you need a game for toddlers/preschoolers that is guaranteed to teach taking turns and highly giggle inducing, then Pop up Pirate is your game!
text_fidelity_b: Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+

These decks are simply the cards taken out of the Pokemon Acadamy starter set, and the Pokemon Go decks, but without any of the extra items. It's a better value to buy them from their proper sets, but if you don't care about the extras, then this product is cheaper, and adds in some value in the way of mystery. If that's your thing.

Overall, for a mystery Pokemon deck set, I think this was actually good. Not phenomenal, but good and probably a good gift for anyone that doesn't have any decks to play with. My only real complaint is this, it does not come with rules, and so you need to look them up online to learn to play, if you don't already know. However, Pokemon give these for free online, and they are much more in depth than any of the printed rules anyway.

text_fidelity_a: LEGO City Police Helicopter Chase 60243 Police Playset, Building Sets for Kids (212 Pieces) Playability is great for a kid with several mini figures and an assortment of vehicles. I’m not a fan of the new helicopter. It is more of a hazard than anything. It doesn’t “glide” or “fly” well. It comes off the stand and shoots quickly to the ground. It’d be more enjoyable if it was just a standard LEGO helicopter that involved more build and more imagination to play than chasing down the helicopter after you pull the rip cord and hoping it doesn’t hit anyone on its way down. It also seems like a lame gimmick to “be more interactive” or something. Otherwise the set is cool. The ATV and motorcycle are neat, sturdy builds. The police semi is cool looking but has a glaring aesthetics flaw. The roof above the driver does not connect flush to the windshield. Instead it overhangs over the windshield. It looks sloppy and more like a flaw than an intentional look. Aside from that it looks great and was fun to build. The trailer is sleek. It has neat folding arms for holding the helicopter in place and the rip cord and stand all attach discreetly to the trailer. It all looks great together, but I still think the rip cord feature is kinda lame and the set could have more police accoutrements on the trailer or a better helicopter that has more playability. Price is about what I would expect.

Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange This is a simple "flick-and-write" game with good production values, a questionable rulebook, simple and fast gameplay, and a box that is just ridiculously large for what it is.

Gameplay is fast and straightforward, involving a Crokinole style mechanism for shooting your disc into a recessed game board with a central hole in the middle. This board has a plastic shelf with corner sections for "shooting" pieces, and they'll fall into a central area divided into four main sections. My central board easily comes loose from the shelving piece, and needs to be adjusted prior to gameplay almost all the time. Once you shoot, you'll be making marks onto your player board with the included markers, which are of average quality for a game like this. The boards are easily erasable - a major plus to the production aspect of the game.

The rules are not that hard, but they are explained in a way that makes learning the game quite a bit more difficult than it needs to be. Few examples are covered, and there will be a number of times that you run into situations where you aren't sure how to interpret the rule as written. Once you get it though, play is not too hard, and Sonora is something you can play with the kids after you've worked out the kinks. And they'll want to play this - it's colorful, with kid-friendly artwork, and the gameplay looks like a kid's game, but has enough meat to interest an adult for at least a little while. I don't know that I'd play this game too often, but it is certainly different and a good family game that will keep kids interested. You can play a few games back to back, as they'll run 20 minutes or so once you know the general flow of the game. For a family game night, this will be a good alternative to a more traditional strategy or roll-and-move board game.

The biggest downfall of this one is that the box is so large. As a gamer with a large collection, it's disappointing to see a 12x12 "Ticket to Ride" sized box for a game that could have opted for a foldable game board and fit into a very small game box. They would have lost nothing in doing this, and in fact, they might have fixed the issue I have with the main board. Even if they must have a one-piece board, dropping the molded plastic insert that holds a handful of discs and pens could have reduced the size by a few inches in depth. In reality, there's not much here in the box, and the components can be entirely stored in the recessed game board area alone. That would be about 3/4" in depth, not 3".

All in all, it's OK.
text_fidelity_b: Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder System Stunt Kit Playset This HOT WHEELS TRACK BUILDER SYSTEM STUNT KIT is one of the best "stunt kits" yet, because it can be set up in any of four (4) different gravity-defying configurations. You build a basic "stunt base", then choose the build that suits your numbered experience level: High Jump (1), Criss Cross (2), Long Jump (3), or The Drop (4). If you tire of one of the builds, you can easily take it apart and rebuild it into a different one. (The stunt pictured on the box is the High Jump.)

Because I'm experienced with the Track Builder System, I chose to build the Long Jump. (I passed on The Drop for now, because it requires a tabletop as well as floor space for the setup.) This is a high-performance stunt--you load a car into the rubber-band-powered launcher, hit the launcher release disk hard, and send the car up a ramp, around a loop-de-loop, over a wide gap to a ramp landing, and then down the track to exit the stunt into the rest of your Track Builder layout. You can use the "measuring stick" to measure and lengthen the gap (the distance to the ramp), once you master the launching technique needed to send the car through the entire stunt to a successful completion.

Unfortunately, this stunt kit is also one of the most difficult to build. The Hot Wheels instructions are always a bit confusing--the drawings are three-dimensional, but they lack the dimensional accuracy of LEGO drawings. The parts are shown in the instructions in their actual plastic colors, which helps, but the drawings don't always make it easy to identify the shapes of the parts or to see exactly how they go together. However, the Building Instructions and parts for this kit have a feature I don't remember seeing before: letters (A, B, C, etc.) molded into the parts, so you can match the letters (A to A; B to B: etc.) to connect the parts. This, too, helps with the building stage. (Always remember that if you can't get the car to complete the stunt--no matter how hard you try--you probably made a mistake in the build.)

The parts in the "stunt base" (see my first photo below) click together very tightly, and more or less permanently. I was unable to pry the parts apart, even using workshop tools. As a result, the assembled stunt kit cannot be taken completely apart for flat storage in the original box.

This stunt kit comes with only one Hot Wheels car, and you will need at least one more car to fully play with it. All four configurations have suggestions for using two cars (crashing at track crossings, comparing speeds, etc.). The kit has two (2) extremely powerful 4-speed launchers--I love these! The launchers are the best I've ever seen. (They are already set up when you take them out of the box--don't fool with the rubber bands.) Another new wrinkle in this Stunt Kit is that you can use the retail box itself to add interest and difficulty to your larger Track Builder System layout. There are printed ramps and "fire pits" that can be pushed up and locked together to make a platform with more obstacles for the cars.

This is an excellent choice for any Track Builder System layout, because of its versatility, economical use of floor space, and low price (about $24 on Amazon). The only drawback is that it's harder to build than most Hot Wheels stunts.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder System Stunt Kit Playset

Parentswell Inflatable Mermaid Pool Floats, 71'' Swimming Pool Tube Mermaid Floaties, Huge Pool Float for Adults, Mermaid Swim Tubes for Pool Party Lounge Birthday Gift Having an inground pool means constantly looking for ways to enhance the experience. We don’t do much actual swimming in our pool. We mainly hang out and float, so having pool floats is a necessity. A recent addition to our backyard recreation was this inflatable Mermaid Pool Float from Parentswell.

Pulling this float from the package and unfolding it, you can see that it’s going to be larger than most, and it is. The lengthy tail is the reason. Inflating it will require a powerful set of lungs, since it is larger than average. I didn’t have a suitable pump for mine, so I did have to inflate the old- fashioned way. It took time, but I got there.

Once inflated, it was ready to test in the pool. The opening in the middle is narrow enough that you can either lie on top of the float without worry that you will fall through. Or, you can stick your body through the center and wear the float, as you drift around in your pool. It works as well as any and the mermaid design is certainly cute. In fact, I would say that the cuteness factor is possibly it’s strongest point. It will be a huge hit with anyone who love mermaids.

Pools are better when you have things to enhance the experience. This float from Parentswell is a good one overall. It can take time to inflate but once ready, it holds its own and it does look cute inside my inground pool.

It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.

dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks The theme for my five-year old's birthday party was Lego Batman. Therefore, I needed a bunch of Lego bricks to make decorations, but I did not want to pay an expensive Lego price and I also just needed basic bricks and colors. Enter the Dreambuilder Toy Building Bricks with 1000 bricks! Not only did I get exactly what I wanted, but I also got a superior toy. I was able to "build" all the decorations I needed (a napkin and silverware holder) with lots of bricks to spare, but when the party was over, I gave my son all the bricks and he was none the wiser that these were not "real" Legos. Some of the older boys at the party inspected the decorations and were able to come to a conclusion that these were in fact not real Legos, but that does not matter because they function exactly like real Legos.

Within the bag you get basic bricks in various sizes, 1x1, 2x2, 2x6, 2x8, etc. There is also one small, green building plate. The set also comes with various bricks for roofs, doors, fences, and windows. The colors are Roy G. Biv with black, white, and grey added. There are equal amounts of each color. We do have a real Lego 1000 piece "creative" bucket and here are the differences. There is no idea booklet with this. However, I do believe you can check their website for building ideas. Therefore, if free form building is not for your child like it is for mine, then this set is not for you. There is no brick separator, and the really flat bricks that drove us adults insane when we were kids are back to haunt to us. You will need to purchase one separately unlike the Lego creative sets. The Lego creative sets have more unique bricks, which take away from having more basic bricks to build bigger and better things as you would with this set. Dreambuilder bricks do not come with a storage bucket. You will receive a plastic bag with all of the bricks contained within that bag. So, you will need your own storage box.

Overall, I find the Dreambuilder bricks to be vastly superior to Lego if you are into simple, old school, free building without instructions. I will be purchasing additional sets.
text_fidelity_b: dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks

B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z Toddlers love to play and they benefit from toys that encourage learning or help in other areas of development. One toy that seems promising in these ways is the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers.

This puzzle has knobs on the pieces, making it easy for toddlers to grab each piece. It helps with coordination, too, as little ones will learn to fit the right shape into the right slot. However, the colors of the pieces are washed out and they really need to be an eye catching primary. Not only would it be more inviting to toddlers and preschoolers but it would provide an opportunity to not only teach numbers and counting, but color recognition too while playing.

Another issue with the pieces is that the details are lacking. If you are going to add detail make it something a child can recognize. But probably the most shocking oversight is the shapes and numbers that they are supposed to match. There is an octagon, for example, that represents the number 7, a five- pointed star that is used for the number 8, and so on. Why would you do this? The octagon should be the number 8 and the star should match with number 5. This is an oversight that someone should have caught.

Other issues I have are with the puzzle holes- they are a little too big and this would be hard to travel anywhere with. I do like that the numbers are nice and big and easy to see and that the knobs are big and tall enough for tiny fingers to grasp. While I haven’t seen it happen yet I do worry because, since they are very much like thumbtacks, they may come loose and eventually get lost. The pieces don’t hold in place as well as I would like.

Toddler toys that help kids learn are nice and while the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers does help with coordination and other skills, it lacks in other areas. The oversight with the numbers and shapes not matching is a big one and I have other issues, too. So, when I think of everything as a whole, this toy gets a thumbs down from me.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z

Animoodles Magnetic Hazel Sloth Stuffed Animal Plush, 7.5" , Brown Many stuffed plush toys that are equipped with joints are difficult to pose. Using magnets in the place of joints makes posing your stuffie very easy. There are currently 14 different Animoodles Magnetic Stuffed Animal Plush toys. Most popular animals among today's current toy trends are available. The plush material is incredibly soft and the embroidered features are incredibly cute. We were able to have Kylie the Cat join our household. Her limbs were each held into place with a plastic tab, which was not difficult to clip and remove completely.

Kylie came with a booklet that tells the origin story of the Animoodles with small written profiles and photos of each toy in the series. There are also practical safety warnings regarding the magnets used in the plush.

I had some concerns about magnets in a child's toy, but the smallest magnet I can feel through the fabric is about the size of a nickle. The stitching is solid, it would be difficult to remove the magnets. Kylie has a lemon bow stitched onto her head, the colors are very cohesive. The pupil of the eyes are buttons. I would strongly advise this toy to not be available to any child under 3 or any other children that are prone to putting random objects into their mouth or being overly destructive with their toys. The button eyes and internal magnets are simply not safe for babies, toddlers or destructive children, as it's made clear in the attached booklet.

The Animoodles Magnetic Stuffed Animal Plush would make a great gift for many children. However, Kylie was in a sealed plastic bag inside the shipping box, so this may be a gift that is better to present in a gift bag rather than wrapping unless you opt to use the shipping box. Play would be expanded with more Animoodles from the series. Additional Animoodles allow for any sort of crazy plush hybrid desired.

My favorite features of the Animoodles is the creative construction and the softness of the plush material. This would make a great addition to any plush animal collection.
text_fidelity_b: Animoodles Magnetic Hazel Sloth Stuffed Animal Plush, 7.5" , Brown

text_fidelity_a:
Kiddieland Lights 'N' Sounds Space Blaster,Multi Perfect item for toddlers who are stuck in that quirky place.. between infant toys not peaking or holding their interest yet, toddler toys are a bit cognitively too hard!! At 18mo. This is the perfect size being its lower profile.. for a little to play without your help! They can climb on/off and scoot a few feet.. if they tumble or bump off, no worry of injury with adult supervision and used on carpet.

Ours is entertained by anything he can load and unload on his own.. Ohh, and pushable buttons seem just too much for him!! This space blaster delivers in spades.. he’ll mount up scoot a few ft. all just to get up and meticulously load in items around the house into the seat! Then, repeat the process stop- and time to unload his haul! Before each scoot.. he moves through a button sequence with the gadgets provided on the dash… he even removes spaceman and puts into the seat- filling up the “under the hood” as well.. This $38 item has provided us our longest entertainment yet at this awkward stage.

Downside components noticed: this does not have a mute button!!! If turned on you get both lights ans sounds- Would love ability without sound when using dash controls- as the sounds get daunting!! I recommend indoor use only and although this can in theory function outdoors.. I find it’s not made for outside elements! Concrete rips up plastic tires fast and any water sprinkler, rain, etc will bring it to an early demise..!! (If used outdoors place on grass + bring inside after use!)

A quirky toy for that awkward phase and one I’d recommend.. it’s not the element of riding that entertains- but, rather what can be done while maneuvering!! Hoping this info can help your decision- stay safe.
text_fidelity_b: Kiddieland Lights 'N' Sounds Space Blaster,Multi

Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+ Mixed feelings on this one.

It can maybe speed up wrapping bracelets, necklaces, etc. But it also requires some patience and if you try to go too fast, you're just going to make a mess of things. So, honestly, you won't be going much faster than if doing this by hand. If you want a thicker cord it can be tricky to fit it through the holding slot (tip - instead of going through the slot on the top, go through the bottom).

Making anything longer than a bracelet will also take some serious patience and practice as it requires sliding your work up and therefore tying your already worked piece into place / slide it through the holding slot.

Once you get the hang of it, it does feel like this is almost a third hand. It's a great way to manage the cords while you work but it's definitely not going to be worth it for most people. It doesn't feel like the game changer that their Loopdeloom did. For me it's helpful as I do have problems with my hands at times. But for the kids that this is targeting, this is probably more trouble than it's worth.
text_fidelity_b: Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+

text_fidelity_a:
My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set This is a fun little train set for toddlers. The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. It comes in a handy carry bag with large plastic track pieces and two toys: Thomas the Tank Engine and Harold the Helicopter. Not quite sure why they include a helicopter to roll around a train track, but I suppose he is one of the more popular characters in Thomas' world. Regardless, they are both cute and large enough for a toddler to get his hands on and push around the track.

Thomas and Harold come attached to a piece of cardboard which keeps them in place. Before you go crazy on how to get these off - after a bit of struggling myself, I realized that all you have to do is rotate the plastic tab things that are holding them in place (located on the bottom). Just turn the tabs 90 degrees (doesn't matter which way) to free Thomas and Harold.

You will definitely need to help your put this together as the track pieces have a snug fit. they may loosen with time, however. There are instructions on how to put the track together, though I'm sure you can figure out your own unique layouts as well. The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

This is a really fun little set with a a nice carry bag to store all the pieces and even take the set with you on adventures. Little ones will love it!
text_fidelity_b: My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set
